hypotheses.statement: The checkout API 5xx spike was caused by the expired payments-gateway.internal certificate, which prevented TLS handshakes and caused payments.authorize calls to timeout
The release 2026.5.14-a was not the cause of the incident, as it contained no code changes on the checkout submit path and the system recovered before the rollback completed
The temporal proximity of the release (09:09:52Z) to the certificate expiration (09:11:40Z) and TLS failures (09:11:47Z) led responders to incorrectly attribute the incident to the release

observed_facts.statement: payments connector TLS handshake failures began at 09:11:47Z with 'certificate verify failed: certificate has expired' error
checkout submit requests returned 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted retries
The checkout-api error ratio reached 0.184 (objective 0.005) and latency p99 reached 10400ms (client timeout)
A trace shows payments.authorize span timing out after 10388ms with no upstream response
The release 2026.5.14-a contained only email template changes and CSV export dependency bump, with no code on the checkout submit path
payments connector TLS handshakes succeeded again at 09:57:55Z after certificate rotation took effect at 09:57:50Z
The error ratio recovered to 0.004 at 09:58:10Z, before the rollback completed at 10:04:18Z
The incident ticket was resolved with note 'rolled back and recovered' without mentioning the certificate issue

summary: A 46-minute checkout API outage was caused by an expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal, not by the coincidentally timed release 2026.5.14-a. The certificate expired at 09:11:40Z, causing TLS handshake failures starting at 09:11:47Z that prevented payments authorization. This led to 502 errors and elevated 5xx ratio (0.184 vs 0.005 objective) until certificate rotation at 09:57:50Z restored connectivity. The system recovered before the unnecessary rollback completed, and the incident ticket incorrectly attributed resolution to the rollback rather than the certificate fix.

timeline.statement: checkout-api release 2026.5.14-a deployed to production with copy edits to email templates and CSV export dependency bump
payments-gateway.internal leaf certificate expired (per payments-gateway team report)
payments connector TLS handshake failures begin with 'certificate verify failed: certificate has expired' error
checkout submit requests start returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausts retries
checkout-api error ratio alert fires with 5xx ratio of 0.184 (objective 0.005)
checkout-api latency alert fires with p99 latency rising to 10400ms (client timeout)
INC-7742 opened with title 'Checkout submit failing for all customers', no impact estimate recorded
Responder attributes incident to the recent release and suggests rollback
Trace shows checkout submit taking 10402ms with payments.authorize span timing out after 10388ms
Responder disputes release causation, points to payments connector TLS failures and expired certificate
payments connector TLS handshakes succeed again, error rate returns to baseline
checkout-api error ratio alert recovers (5xx ratio 0.004)
Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed (after recovery)
INC-7742 marked resolved with note 'rolled back and recovered', no mention of certificate issue
